To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peripheral priming of cytotoxic T lymphocytes by melanocyte-associated antigene directly presented in lymph node melanobasts can be a major factor for tolerance induction to self-antigents in the periphery and may constitute a major advantage for immunotherapeutic approaches based on T-cell transfer.

the promiscuous expression and presentation of self-antigen is necessary for peripheral tolerance, because the same self-antigen can directly be presented in the periphery and induce cytotoxic T cells.

promiscuous expression in the medulla of the thymus and peripheral presentation of a self-antigen by lymph node melanocyte precursors are complementary mechanisms for the establishment of CD8(+)T cell tolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of self-tolerance and its failure in autoimmune diseases and cancer.
the mechanisms of central tolerance and the role of the thymus in the generation of peripheral immunity.
the question, how the immune system can tolerate self and still be able to react against non-self antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the peripheral presentation of a self antigen in a lymph node can induce CD8+ T-cell tolerance or priming depending on the nature of the antigen, and on the presence of other factors such as costimulation, cytokine milieu, and the presence of antigen-presenting cells.
the thymic expression of self antigens is not only a necessary but also an important mechanism to induce tolerance.
peripheral tolerance is not the default mechanism, but rather the exception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peripheral presentation of the self antigen is a mandatory, but not a superfluous mechanism, to counteract the priming of high affinity T cells in the periphery.

the promiscuous expression in the thymic medulla of self-antigenic peptides that can also be directly presented in the periphery, such as the melanocyte-associated antigents, is a mechanism that ensures that the periphery is not primed by these antigens.
the promiscuous expression in the thymic medulla of self-antigen is a mandatory rather than a superfluos mechanism to counteract peripheral self-priming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peripheral priming by melanoblasts may constitute an advantage of adoptive T-cell therapies based on CD8(+) cytotoxic T cells.
peripheral priming of T cells can occur in lymph nodes and that this priming is not restricted to the thymus.
promiscuous expression in the thymic medulla is a mechanism that prevents peripheral priming of high-affinity CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell clones by the same antigens expressed in the periphery.
